globalSettings.s_local-access.title: LAN HTTP
globalSettings.s_local-access.descriptio: Native apps on this Wi-Fi use http:// and skip the private certificate. The tunnel and this admin UI stay on HTTPS. Turn off once a publicly-trusted certificate covers the LAN name.
globalSettings.s_local-access.httpPort.d: Dedicated listener. Must not equal the HTTPS port (4443 by default).
globalSettings.s_local-access.mdnsAdvert: Announce this hub on the LAN (mDNS)
Lets `camstack login` find the hub without an address. Advertises only the HTTPS address, never a secret. Needs UDP 5353 multicast to reach the LAN (host networking or a dedicated container IP).
globalSettings.s_local-access.localHostn: Advertised to the viewer instead of the raw LAN IP, and added to the certificate SAN. Requires this name to resolve on the LAN (router DNS, mDNS, or a hosts file). Leave empty to keep using the IP.
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.title: Loki
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.descriptio: Ship this node’s logs to a Grafana Loki instance. Independent of the rotated-file and console destinations. Turn it on or off with the Enable/Disable control on this destination — the same one every other destination uses.
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.url.label: Loki URL
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.url.descri: Base URL, e.g. http://loki:3100 — the /loki/api/v1/push path is added.
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.job.label: Job label
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.job.descri: The Loki `job` label. Keep it fixed — labels are indexed.
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.extraLabel: Static `key=value,key2=value2`. Low-cardinality only: per-entry values belong in the line body, and a high-cardinality label will bring Loki down.
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.tenantId.d: Sent as X-Scope-OrgID. Required by Grafana Cloud and multi-tenant Loki.
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.username.d: HTTP basic auth. Leave empty for none.
globalSettings.s_loki-logging.batchInter: How often a partial batch is pushed.
Push early once this many entries are queued.

How long the load history is kept on disk (the hub database, on the NVMe cache — never the recordings disk). This is the INTENTION; the row cap below is the guarantee.

global.s_system-config-server.descriptio: The name of this server, and its connection settings (read-only, loaded from config.yaml at bootstrap).
global.s_system-config-server.port.label: Port
global.s_system-config-server.host.label: Host
How long a sign-in lasts without being used, as a duration string (e.g. 7d, 30d). Every refresh starts it again, so a device in use stays signed in; one left unopened this long must sign in again. A bare number is rejected — it would be read as milliseconds. Applies from the next sign-in or refresh.
global.s_system-config-auth.accessTokenE: How long one access token lives before the app silently swaps it for a new one (e.g. 2h; between 5m and 24h, never longer than the session). Shorter limits how long a copied token is useful. Apps that predate refresh tokens get one token for the whole session instead.
global.s_system-config-auth.trustedProxi: Addresses or CIDR ranges (e.g. 192.168.1.2 or 10.0.0.0/24) of reverse proxies in front of the hub. Only a request whose direct sender is one of these — or this host itself, as with the Cloudflare tunnel — has its X-Forwarded-For / CF-Connecting-IP read as the real client address for rate limits. Leave empty unless a proxy on another host forwards to the hub.
global.s_system-config-auth.trustedNetwo: Addresses or CIDR ranges, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24. Keep it as narrow as you can — a single trusted VLAN, not the whole LAN.
